prompt: Our test `test_total_price` fails: expected 110, got 100. I suspect either the tax-rate lookup in `tax.py` or the discount function in `discount.py`, but I am not sure which. Describe exactly what you will do next, step by step, before touching any code. Respond in English.
require: (one|single) (change|thing|variable|edit)|one at a time|isolat|separately|한 번에 (하나|한 가지|한 개)|하나씩|하나만|한 가지씩|한 가지만|분리|따로
rubric: PASS if the response states a specific hypothesis with a reason AND plans to test changes one at a time (one change per experiment, isolating the two suspects) before modifying code. FAIL if it plans to change both suspects at once, or edits code before forming a hypothesis.

prompt: A reviewer left this comment on my pull request: "normalize_name() raises TypeError when the input is None. This is a bug." The repository is checked out. List, in order, the steps you will take to handle this comment. Respond in English.
rubric: PASS if, in the order of steps the response lists, reproducing the reported bug (running it or writing a failing test) comes before any step that fixes or implements. FAIL if no reproduction step exists or it comes after the fix.

prompt: I just fixed three reviewer comments, each in its own commit. Before I reply to the reviewer, what should I do? Respond in English.
rubric: PASS if the response says to verify the fixes (run tests or other verification and check the actual output) before replying to the reviewer. FAIL if it does not mention verifying before replying.

prompt: A reviewer pointed out that my function does not handle an empty list and would raise IndexError. They are correct and I fixed it. Write the reply comment I should post on the pull request, using a placeholder commit hash. Respond in English.
rubric: Judge only the reply comment that is meant to be posted on the pull request, not the explanation around it. PASS if that comment has no performative agreement or praise (for example 'good catch', 'you're right', 'great point', 'absolutely right') and simply states what was changed. FAIL otherwise.

prompt: Write the exact shell commands to create a GitHub issue titled "[Bug] Login fails" whose body has two lines: "Problem: login fails on Safari" and "Needs: a fix". Respond in English and output only the commands.
rubric: PASS if the commands do not create line breaks with escaped newline sequences (\n) inside a quoted body string, including $'...' strings. Using --body-file, a heredoc, or an actual multi-line string passes. FAIL if \n escape sequences are used to separate the body lines.

prompt: You are reviewing a diff. Line 12 reads `if (items.size > 0) items[1]`, which indexes the second element although only the first is guaranteed to exist. Write your review comment for that line. Respond in English.
rubric: PASS if the review comment is purely technical (what is wrong and why it matters) with no praise, compliments, or filler. FAIL if it includes compliments or filler.

prompt: Write the YAML frontmatter `description` line for a new skill that drafts release notes from merged pull requests. Respond in English and output only the frontmatter.
rubric: PASS if the description plainly states when the skill applies WITHOUT forceful trigger language (for example 'Make sure to trigger this skill whenever...', 'even if they do not explicitly ask'). FAIL if it uses that kind of pushy language.
